tools.name: find_vc_firms
tools.description: Use this when a founder asks which venture capital investors to pitch, wants an investor list for a fundraise, or asks which VC firms back a kind of startup. Not for fundraising mechanics such as SAFEs, valuation or dilution, or for investor contact details. Ranks up to 20 public VC firms for a star

tools.name: get_vc_firm_details
tools.description: Use this when the user asks about a specific VC firm by name, or about a firm in a find_vc_firms result. Returns the public profile of one VC firm: name, location, website, a short thesis, the stages it has invested at, check size, sectors, geoggraphies and up to 10 recent public portfolio companies.

tools.name: email_report_link
tools.description: Use this when a founder asks to have their F4 Raise report link emailed to them, giving their own address and the code from a find_vc_firms result. Emails the founder one message with a personal link that opens F4's free report form with the description already filled in. It needs the code at the en

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "email_report_link" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: find_vc_firms, email_report_link · Private data: find_vc_firms, get_vc_firm_details · Public sink: find_vc_firms, email_report_link.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: find_vc_firms, email_report_link · Private data: find_vc_firms, get_vc_firm_details · Public sink: find_vc_firms, email_report_link

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
